articles.title: Premier League pre-season predictions 2026/27: Sky Sports supercomputer tips Arsenal to retain title - Between the Lines
articles.summary: The title race, the fight for the Champions League spots and the battle to avoid relegation are assessed as the Sky Sports supercomputer predicts the 2026/27 Premier League table. Where is your team tipped to finish in the campaign ahead?
articles.body:
As the new Premier League season draws closer, featuring 215 games to be shown live on Sky Sports , we've fired up the Sky Sports supercomputer to predict the final table.

Find out where your team finishes as we take a look at the risers and fallers in Between the Lines , the Sky Sports strand unpicking the data behind the biggest stories in football.

Our predicted table, which is based on 10,000 simulations and factors historic performance, transfer business and betting odds, has Arsenal as champions for a second year running.

The Gunners, champions for the first time in 22 years, are tipped to become only the fourth side in Premier League history to retain the crown after Manchester United, Manchester City, and Chelsea.

Their expected points total of 85.2 is almost identical to their title-winning 85-point haul last season and puts them nearly four points clear of Manchester City , who are predicted to be runners-up again as they begin a new era following Pep Guardiola's departure.

City, who have signed Elliot Anderson for a club-record £116m fee, are predicted to finish closer to Arsenal than last season, when they lagged seven points behind. The supercomputer also expects improvement from Liverpool , where Andoni Iraola has taken over following a fifth-placed finish under Arne Slot.

The Reds are predicted to climb two places to third, with an expected points total of 76.8, putting them just ahead of Manchester United , who are predicted to drop a place to fourth despite finishing last season strongly under Michael Carrick.

Chelsea , whose list of summer signings includes the £117m they paid for Morgan Rogers, as well as a new manager in Xabi Alonso, are predicted to climb five places to fifth, ahead of sixth-placed Spurs , who are tipped to climb 11 places following a summer of transfer spending.

Aston Villa are predicted to drop out of the Champions League places and finish seventh, with Bournemouth , Brighton and Brentford completing the predicted top half.

At the other end of the table, the Sky Sports supercomputer predicts newly-promoted sides Coventry , Ipswich and Hull will go straight back down to the Championship.

Frank Lampard's Coventry are tipped to mount the strongest survival challenge, with an expected points total only fractionally lower than Nottingham Forest's.

Forest, 16th-placed finishers last term, have appointed former Crystal Palace boss Oliver Glasner as their new head coach but are predicted to finish a place below his old club in 17th.

Newcastle are also expected to endure another difficult season. The Magpies slumped to a disappointing 12th-placed finish last term. Following a turbulent summer in which they have sold key players Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon and replaced Eddie Howe with Matthias Jaissle, they are predicted to come 13th.

The only positive for Newcastle is that they are predicted to finish ahead of rivals Sunderland , who will come 15th this season, according to the Sky Sports supercomputer, despite achieving an historic seventh-placed finish last season.

Everton , up from 13th to 11th, are the only team in our bottom half with a predicted position for the new season higher than their actual finishing position last term. The other spots in the bottom half are taken by Fulham , in 12th, and Leeds , in 14th.

Title and relegation probabilities compared

Adding probability percentages to the predicted table provides further context on the title, top four and relegation battles.

Arsenal's 50.6 per cent chance of winning the title, according to the Sky Sports supercomputer, is nearly twice as high as any other side's, underlining their status as strong favourites.

With a 27.5 per cent chance, Manchester City are deemed far more likely winners than Liverpool on 10.2 per cent. Manchester United , meanwhile are only given a 7.3 per cent title chance. Chelsea are given a 3.9 per cent chance, with Spurs next on 0.4 per cent.

Aston Villa have upset the established order by finishing in the top four in two of the last three seasons, but they are only given a 3.6 per cent chance of repeating the feat this season, with Arsenal, City, Liverpool and Manchester United strongly fancied by the supercomputer and Chelsea and Spurs the only other contenders.

Hull , promoted through the play-offs following a sixth-placed Championship finish last season, are given a massive 81.6 chance of relegation, far higher than next-highest Ipswich on 47.5 per cent.

Nottingham Forest , meanwhile, are given the same chance of relegation as Coventry on 43.1 per cent. Crystal Palace and Sunderland are rated at 32.8 per cent and 22.4 per cent respectively to go down, ahead of Leeds on nine per cent.

The 2026/27 Premier League season begins with Arsenal vs Coventry live on Sky Sports on Friday August 21; kick-off 8pm

articles.title: Ryan Fitzpatrick goes off on Bo Nix after Broncos beat Seahawks on ‘Thursday Night Football’
articles.summary: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix threw for 107 yards on four yards per attempt, while Denver punted on six straight drives in the second half. But Seattle S...
articles.body:
Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix threw for 107 yards on four yards per attempt, while Denver punted on six straight drives in the second half. But Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold tossed a back-breaking interception in overtime, allowing the Broncos to escape with a 17-14 win on Thursday Night Football .

Denver's defense may have bailed Nix out, but Ryan Fitzpatrick didn't let him off the hook during Prime Video's postgame broadcast.

"I'm glad they scored the two touchdowns in the first half, but they were in four-minute mode when the second half started," Fitzpatrick said. "It was really frustrating to watch. And part of it, for me, is Bo Nix is not playing competitively. It's almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he's playing football right now."

Fitzpatrick elaborated on exactly why he's so disgusted, saying, "First of all, the guy doesn't want to throw the ball. That's fine. He's throwing to the flats, he's throwing behind, but he has no trust from his coach."

"In overtime, he's got two chances to be competitive," Fitzpatrick said. "The last one being a designed run for him to run, make somebody miss, and get a first down for your football team! Now, they're in the locker room right now. They're excited. They won. He's not playing competitive football right now."

Fitzpatrick wasn't alone in his criticisms of Nix, as Tony Gonzalez jumped in to note that "the only thing that's protecting him, obviously, is the wins" and Denver's dominant defense.

"Offensively right now, it is anemic," Gonzalez said. "If I'm a Denver Bronco fan, I'm looking at this going, hey, if this keeps up, maybe even a good benching. I'm just saying. To get your attention, to put [Jarrett] Stidham in there or something, because right now, offensively, you cannot be happy about this."

Earlier this week, Nix addressed the mounting criticism over his poor play to start the 2026 NFL season.

"Playing good and playing bad, it's a narrative, and I think it's honestly kind of something we make up," Nix told reporters . "I don't think necessarily I'm playing any different than what I'm normally playing."

Dating back to last season, the prevailing narrative about Nix has been that the Broncos' defense is carrying him, and both the eye test and statistics objectively back that up. Yet, much to the talking heads' chagrin, Nix and the Broncos sit at 4-2.

Denver will visit the Arizona Cardinals (1-4) in Week 7.

articles.title: Los Angeles Dodgers’ Dave Roberts Drops Blunt Quote After Brewers’ NLCS Sweep
articles.summary: Dodgers manager Dave Roberts dropped a blunt quote after getting eliminated from the playoffs by the Brewers in the NLCS. The post Los Angeles Dodgers’ Dave...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers won't three-peat as World Series Champions.

The Milwaukee Brewers completed a 4-0 sweep of the Dodgers in the National League Championship Series with a 6-4 win at Dodger Stadium on Thursday.

The Brewers will play the winner of the American League Championship Series between the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays in the Fall Classic.

After being eliminated, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts dropped a blunt quote.

Los Angeles Dodgers Manager Dave Roberts Drops Blunt Quote After Milwaukee Brewers' NLCS Sweep

Dave Roberts says he has no regrets about this series.

"I think at the end of the day, we got beat. We got outplayed in all facets. Those guys played flawless. Defensively, they pitched better than we did, they hit better than we did, they slugged better than we did."

Milwaukee Brewers Complete Sweep of Los Angeles Dodgers With 6-4 Win

Third baseman David Hamilton went 2-for-4 with a home run, an RBI single and two runs scored as the Brewers beat the Dodgers 6-4 at Dodger Stadium on Thursday.

Left-hander Shane Drohan served as the opener for the Brewers. He allowed one earned run in one inning.

Dustin May relieved Drohan and allowed three earned runs over three innings.

After May, JoJo Romero threw two scoreless innings, and Aaron Ashby hurled three shutout innings.

In the second inning, Andy Pages hit an RBI single, and Shohei Ohtani hit a three-run home run to give the Dodgers a 4-0 lead.

Jake Bauers cut the Dodgers' lead to two with a two-run double in the fourth inning

In the fifth inning, Hamilton hit an RBI single, and Jake Bauers walked in the tying run.

Garrett Mitchell hit a go-ahead home run in the top of the sixth inning. Hamilton hit a solo home run in the ninth inning to make the score 6-4.

Tyler Glasnow made the start for Los Angeles, allowing four runs over 4 1/3 innings. The Dodgers used four other pitchers after Glasnow.

articles.title: Dion Dublin tells Manchester United to sign Harry Kane: ‘If you want him, go get him’
articles.summary: FC Bayern is not letting Harry Kane leave any time soon.
articles.body:
Former Manchester United and England striker Dion Dublin believes his old club should stop talking about signing Harry Kane and make a move for the Bayern Munich superstar, arguing that the England captain would improve any Premier League side.

Speaking to BetVictor , Dublin praised Kane's intelligent movement, positional awareness, and extraordinary goalscoring record, insisting that United should be willing to pay whatever it takes to bring him to Old Trafford.

"Harry Kane's contract? Get him down to Cambridge United, we'll have him! Even at 33, 34, 35, I'd still nick Harry for a year or two because he just finds his way into good positions. You put the ball there and he doesn't even have to run about as much," Dublin said. "You can see he's dropping into the number 10 role a bit more, sometimes even into the four, and spraying balls about so he's not easy to mark. Two centre-halves don't know where he is, and then he crops up.

"He's a very clever footballer. I would take Harry Kane right now at Man Utd. There's a bit of a statement in this, Harry Kane could start in any Premier League side. Any Premier League side, it doesn't matter. Every club in the Premier League would take him right now, 100%. United have toyed with it, they've spoken about it too much. If you want him, go get him. Even if he signs a new deal there, give them the 70 or 80 million, whatever they want, because you've got to get goals.

"Why are you buying Harry Kane? To score your goals. Who can you guarantee for goals? Haaland, Kane, Lewandowski, Mbappe, and then you start to struggle a bit for guaranteed scorers. Harry Kane guarantees you goals."

Dublin's argument is straightforward: Manchester United need a reliable goalscorer, and few players in world football offer the consistency Kane brings. The Bayern striker has also developed into much more than a traditional No. 9, using his ability to drop deep, create chances, and dictate play to make himself difficult to defend against.

For United, the question is whether they would be willing to invest heavily in a player approaching the latter stages of his career. Dublin clearly believes the answer should be yes, arguing that Kane's proven quality makes the potential investment worthwhile. With Bayern Munich benefiting from his remarkable output, United fans might wonder what their attack could look like with a striker who makes scoring goals look so routine.

However, a move to Manchester United appears unlikely, with Kane reportedly on course to sign a new contract with Bayern Munich. The England captain has established himself as a key figure in Vincent Kompany's side, and Bayern have every incentive to keep one of the world's most prolific strikers in Munich. Dublin may believe United should do whatever it takes to bring Kane to Old Trafford, but unless the situation changes significantly, the Premier League giants could be left watching as Kane continues his goalscoring exploits in Germany.

articles.title: EFL preview: Swansea and West Ham face off, pressure mounts on Leicester
articles.summary: BBC Sport picks out five things across the EFL that you should be keeping your eyes on this weekend.
articles.body:
The leaves are turning, the shadows of British Summer Time are lengthening and you can't move for Halloween paraphernalia in the shops.

It's a special time of year, not least in the EFL where teams are already jostling for position in the race for promotion, and survival.

We're still a week away from the clocks going back but a glance at the top of the Championship might convince you we've rewound well over a decade already, with seven of the current top nine teams having sat outside the top flight for at least half a dozen seasons, and plenty of them more than double that.

The third tier is also as intriguing as ever while you can pretty much throw your cap over the League Two promotion chasers.

Here are some of the standout fixtures and narratives across the EFL that you should be keeping your eyes on this weekend.

Free-scoring Hammers seek to clip Swans' wings

Game of the weekend? Not going to argue.

Tuesday's last-gasp winner at Millwall made it four straight wins for Swansea either side of the international break to keep the Swans top of the Championship, 16 years since they last won promotion.

Title favourites West Ham, seeking to make an immediate return to the top tier, are four points back in third place after their 6-0 romp at nine-man Lincoln the following night.

The Hammers are the leading scorers across the top four tiers of English football with 29 goals in 10 games, but at 15:00 BST on Saturday will come up against the meanest defence in the division, with Swansea conceding just seven so far.

The Irons have fallen behind in eight of their 13 games in all competitions this season but remain unbeaten in the league on their travels, while the Swans have yet to lose at home, conceding only twice in five games.

Birmingham as the leading West Midlands club? QPR the best in London? Not many would have pegged that as the case after 11 matches of the Championship season, but it could well be the case come Saturday tea-time.

Blues have not been promoted to the Premier League since 2009 but, after drawing their first four home games of the campaign, Chris Davies' side romped to a 4-0 win over lowly Preston on Tuesday to go fourth, making it 10 points from a four-match unbeaten run.

They sit ahead of the fifth-placed Hoops by virtue of goals scored after Julien Stephan's side ended a four-match drawing run by walloping Derby 4-1 on Wednesday.

Rangers, who last went up in 2014, remain unbeaten in five league games on the road, conceding a division-best four goals in that span, and Saturday's result will give us a good idea of which of these sides, if not both, are here to stay in this year's promotion race.

There's no place like home - unless, of course, you're Leicester City.

The Foxes have had a rare week to work on the training pitch, but might have been happier with an away game on Saturday, rather than the visit of Doncaster to the King Power (15:00 BST).

Last Saturday's dismal 3-1 defeat by lowly Peterborough was a third defeat in their past four league games at home - during which they have shipped nine goals - and heaped further pressure on Russell Martin who later said there will be "no quick fix" in sacking him after supporters chanted for his dismissal.

Midfielder John Lundstram also spoke of the team playing with "anxiety" at home and it's worth noting the Foxes remain unbeaten on their travels, where six of their nine points have come.

City lie 17th, one point off the drop zone, and below Rovers on goal difference, with Grant McCann's men having won their past three games in all competitions without conceding.

If you like your promotion chases to be unpredictable, you'll love League One.

Just four points separate the top seven sides in the third tier and any one of four teams could sit top come Saturday evening.

It might have been even closer, had Huddersfield not conceded a 98th-minute equaliser at home to Sheffield Wednesday last time out, which leaves the Terriers three points off the summit before Saturday's (15:00 BST) 600+-mile round trip to leaders Plymouth.

The Pilgrims left it nearly as late to see off AFC Wimbledon last weekend to stay on top, albeit having played a game more, but Saturday looks like an even bigger day with second-placed Bradford hosting Stevenage while Stockport, in third, and Cambridge and Reading, in fifth and sixth respectively, all face sides in the bottom six.

Ammies eye revenge in top v bottom match

If you thought League One was tight, just wait until you hear about League Two.

The top 14 sides are separated by just seven points - indeed leaders Salford and 20th-placed Rotherham are only nine apart after playing 10 matches.

The Ammies will seek to stay at the summit as they host rock-bottom Crawley, with whom they have a fair bit of recent history.

Salford came from 3-2 down with five minutes to play in this fixture last November to win 4-3, but were held to a goalless draw in the return in Sussex on the final day of the regular season which denied City automatic promotion and they eventually lost in the play-off final to Notts County.

Unbeaten Barnet look best placed, sat a point back in second with games in hand before their trip to Tranmere while third-placed Crewe, also unbeaten, welcome Rochdale and Gillingham, in fourth, make the trek to Accrington.

BBC Sport will have live text coverage of all the weekend's EFL action, starting with Burnley v Wolves (20:00 BST) on Friday and throughout Saturday's fixtures across the Championship, League One and League Two.

articles.title: Benfica 4-1 Celtic – Martin O’Neill remains hopeful of qualification
articles.summary: Martin O’Neill remains hopeful of qualification, and praises Celtic duo…Not one Celtic supporter will be feeling confident of the side making strides in Euro...
articles.body:
Martin O'Neill remains hopeful of qualification, and praises Celtic duo…

Not one Celtic supporter will be feeling confident of the side making strides in Europe this year after a second successive loss in the Europa group stages after a 4-1 thumping from Benfica in Lisbon last night.

October 15, 2026, Lisbon, Portugal: Benfica and Celtic players seen during the UEFA Europa League match between Benfica and Celtic at Estadio da Luz. Final score Benfica 4:1 Celtic Lisbon Portugal – Photo Nuno Branco IMAGO

That loss along with the 3-1 home defeat to Ferencvaros leaves us third bottom of the standings, and little hope of making it through to the latter stages.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill however, has came out fighting and is adamant his side can still make an impression in Europe's secondary competition, pointing to the players second half performance as a factor in his belief.

He said: "I thought the second-half performance was really terrific, as you say, a game of two halves.

"We created chance after chance; we should have scored more goals, and of course, you're going to leave yourself a bit open at the end.

"But I tell you, the second-half performance gives me what I would call the determination, I think, to, and I think we can still qualify.

Callum McGregor of Celtic Benfica v Celtic, UEFA Europa League, Football, Estadio da Luz, Lisbon, Portugal – 15 Oct 2026Lisbon Estadio da Luz Portugal Photo Javier Garcia/Shutterstock

Martin was frustrated with the manner of Celtic's early concessions, especially after a missed opportunity to reduce the deficit at 2-0.

He added: "One is just a little dinking cross and we're coming out instead of defending it properly, and that's really poor from our viewpoint. You can't afford to do that.

"I don't think you can afford to do that in any game, never mind a game of this magnitude."

The Irishman was pleased with the performances of substitutes Haissem Hassan and Callum Osmand, and the direction of their approach, which caused Benfica problems.

"It changed because two wide players wanted to get at people, really did want to get at people.

"Hassan has that ability to do this here, and little Osmand, who's just back from injury, hasn't played really wide there at all.

Camilo Duran of Celtic FC looks on during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between SL Benfica vs Celtic FC at Estádio do Lisboa e Benfica on October 15th,2026 Photo by Joao Bravo/Sports IMAGO

"I thought he did terrifically well. Maybe he could have squared one for Duran to maybe make it 3-2 in the game. That would have been really interesting in the last 15 minutes of the match.

"So that gave the rest of the team a bit of impetus."

Despite another damaging European defeat, Martin believes the second half performance can encourage his side in the next round of fixtures.

Asked whether he would take encouragement from it, he replied: "Absolutely, we'll take that.

"Yes, second-half performance I will definitely take."

articles.title: Raúl Varela: "El aterrizaje de Mourinho fue esperanzador, pero al final la cabra suele tirar al monte"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu cuestiona el rendimiento del Real Madrid y exige una reacción tanto al técnico portugués como a Vinicius
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu cuestiona el rendimiento del Real Madrid y exige una reacción tanto al técnico portugués como a Vinicius
articles.body: Raúl Varela ha puesto el foco en José Mourinho y Vinicius en su opinión en La Tribu. El periodista ha analizado el delicado momento que atraviesa el Real Madrid, cuestionando el rendimiento del equipo y reclamando una reacción tanto del entrenador portugués como del futbolista brasileño, que comienza su sanción este domingo frente al Sevilla. "Este domingo y frente al correoso e ilusionante Sevilla de Luis García Plaza comienza la penitencia para Vinicius", arrancó Varela, que no comparte la dureza del castigo: "Un exagerado castigo por una acción liviana en sí y sobre todo comparada con la cantidad de patadas y agresiones alevosas, en bastantes casos premeditadas, que ha tenido que sufrir el número 7 del Madrid". Pese a considerar injusta la sanción, el director de La Tribu cree que el brasileño debe aprovechar esta situación para recuperar su mejor versión. "Esta circunstancia obliga a dos cosas. Una a que Vinicius recapacite, curre, trabaje, cambie y se ponga las pilas", señaló. Varela recordó el rendimiento que llevó al futbolista a convertirse en una de las grandes estrellas del conjunto blanco y lamentó su evolución reciente: "Desde que dijo aquello de 'farei por diez' la cosa no solo no ha multiplicado sino que en muchos aspectos ha dividido y empieza a ser un recuerdo lejano el rendimiento descollante de un futbolista único que ha sido capaz de ganar, casi en solitario, un par de Champions para el Madrid". Pero la crítica de Raúl Varela no se quedó únicamente en Vinicius. El periodista también puso el foco en José Mourinho y en el rendimiento colectivo del Real Madrid. "Luego está lo de Mou, claro. Que no se puede ir de rositas. Su aterrizaje en esta segunda etapa fue esperanzador pero al final la cabra suele tirar al monte y ahora mismo, allí, no todo es orégano", aseguró. Su diagnóstico sobre el juego del equipo fue contundente: "El equipo juega mal, en Roma no fue capaz siquiera de defender bien, se ve sometido en distintos momentos por rivales de todo pelaje y solo la heroica y la calidad individual de algunos futbolistas está sosteniendo el tenderete". Por último, Varela lanzó un aviso al técnico portugués, al que considera obligado a demostrar su capacidad para revertir la situación: "Le llega el momento de tomar decisiones. De gestor y de entrenador". Y cerró su reflexión con un mensaje directo a Mourinho: "Ahora tenemos que chequear si todavía sigue siendo 'special' o por el contrario también debe comprar pilas en el mismo supermercado que Vinicius".

articles.title: FPl tips for gameweek seven: Essential Brighton and Chelsea players?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's FPL expert Gianni Buttice looks at some of the biggest dilemmas facing Fantasy Premier League managers heading into gameweek seven.
articles.body:
BBC Sport's FPL expert Gianni Buttice looks at some of the biggest dilemmas facing Fantasy Premier League managers heading into gameweek seven.

Are Brighton's Maxim de Cuyper and Pascal Gross essential?

They are as close to must-have status as anyone in this game but it would be fair to argue this may not be the best entry point knowing they face Liverpool and Manchester City away in their next three games.

Admittedly Crystal Palace at home in the derby this weekend is a good match-up, but I wouldn't be ripping up my team to accommodate either. Given the choice, I would prioritise defender De Cuyper (£5.1m).

Should I sell Manchester United players?

Bruno Fernandes (£11.9m) is owned by a third of all FPL managers and, as the game's second most expensive asset with five blanks from six, he is an easy sell this week.

Arsenal 's Bukayo Saka (£9.6m) and Chelsea 's Cole Palmer (£9.7m) are both good replacements.

United defenders should also be shipped but there is an argument to hold Bryan Mbeumo (£7.9m) who doesn't break the bank and is ranked equal 10th from all midfielders with 33 points so far this season. He's clearly more of a hold than a buy however.

With an attack-minded manager in Xabi Alonso, no European involvement and a full week on the training ground this Chelsea team look capable of scoring two or three goals every game.

Owning striker Joao Pedro (£7.8m), who is surely now a 'must have' probably isn't enough cover for an attack with such firepower. Choosing between Palmer and Morgan Rogers (£7.9m) isn't easy and probably comes down to budget and your view on how many penalties and set-piece goals Chelsea will score - with Palmer being the main beneficiary.

In open play, there is little to split the inside forwards and Rogers has slightly better underlying data and FPL points from the six games so far.

Should I triple captain Erling Haaland this week?

If you still have the chip, it's worth noting that a double gameweek before gameweek 19, when chips reset, looks unlikely.

Haaland has three standout home fixtures before the end of the year: Ipswich this weekend, Fulham in gameweek 11 and Hull in gameweek 16. There is little to separate them, but Ipswich do not usually sit deep away from home.

They have already lost 5-2 at Manchester United and won 3-2 at Crystal Palace in the league this season.

Who are the best long-term 'set-and-forget' defenders?

De Cuyper has been the standout option, but covering the Arsenal defence also looks sensible.

Under Mikel Arteta, they should remain as the league's best defensive unit, and Riccardo Calafiori (£5.9m) currently looks the strongest route in.

Elsewhere consider your defensive contribution points (defcon) magnets such as Leeds ' Tarik Muharemovic (£5m), Brighton 's Luka Vuskovic (£5.1m), Bournemouth 's Antonio Silva (£5m) and Everton centre-back James Tarkowski (£6.2m).

Not only are all four reliable defcon performers but they all play for solid teams who do not concede too many.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Getting to know Eva Olid
articles.summary: It has been a whirlwind 10 weeks for Eva Olid since she became manager of Manchester United.
articles.body:
It's been a whirlwind 10 weeks for Eva Olid since she became manager of Manchester United.

Her surprise appointment at the start of August after Marc Skinner's departure meant she joined one of the biggest clubs in England just a month before the Women's Super League season started.

When we meet in a Manchester coffee shop - an unlikely setting for someone who doesn't drink coffee - it is her first real pause in a schedule that has left her with little chance to discover the city she now calls home.

"It's been good but really busy," Olid tells BBC Sport. "It's just been work, home, work, home."

Olid, 41, enjoyed exceptional success in her previous role at Hearts - taking them from bottom of the table to Scottish Premier League champions within five years.

Despite that, she was relatively unheard of south of the border, so top of her to-do list when she arrived at the team's training base at Carrington was to explain to her players what she was all about.

"My first day I showed them what I did in the past and who I was," she says. "I tried to be myself from second one. I showed that I'm a person before a coach.

"I didn't have time to be aware of where I was. I just went there, be myself trying to transmit to the players how I see football, to work hard, that I'm going to be there for them, that I want to make them better players. Trying to transmit the key messages that I wanted the players to take from the first moment."

'That week was difficult - a lot of emotions'

Olid's introduction to life at United was far from straightforward.

She inherited a thin squad and new policy of prioritising developing academy players over making signings, while also wanting to implement a new attacking style of football.

It was a big ask. Perhaps too big. In her opening two games, United lost 2-1 at London City Lionesses before a galling 5-0 home defeat by Chelsea.

Olid believes that humbling loss to a title rival - in front of United's own fans - proved to be a turning point in her relationship with the team.

"It was a difficult week," she says. "There were honest conversations. I took responsibility for a lot of things. I think that was a good starting point for the players.

"I was confident. It's crazy to say, I was confident because I knew what the problem was. And when you know the problem, you can change that."

Olid - a defensive midfielder during her playing career, who took pride in doing the simple things well - decided to strip things back.

"I spoke, they spoke, and we knew what we had to do," she says. "That week was difficult - a lot of emotions - but going to Arsenal, we fought for each other, there was hard work. I think it was the perfect starting point for a good moment."

A 1-1 draw at the Emirates was the start of a five-game unbeaten run during which they have climbed from the bottom of the WSL to seventh.

"When you are in Manchester United, you need to find a way to win," she says. "It's a challenge - how you can win and at the same time develop players and at the same time implement a new style of play.

"You need to find the balance of all that together. And I think these last weeks, we got to that point."

Now Olid has settled into her role, she is keen to explore what Manchester has to offer, starting with finding some decent Spanish food.

"I have to say that the tapas... sorry, but some of the tapas bars are not 100% authentic," she says.

"I had this experience in Scotland and I needed time to find a good tapas bar. Because you want it to feel like home. A little taste of home."

Olid admits she has yet to embrace driving on British roads but has become a fan of public transport.

"I was not brave [enough] to drive here," she says. "In Scotland I was moving a lot by bus and here I need to find the ways to move by tram."

And there is one Manchester landmark Olid has already visited: Old Trafford.

"I came 13 years ago to a game - as a fan of football, and what I remember was amazing," she says.

"On Saturday I went for second time and they showed me the changing rooms. The day that we play there this season, I will feel the happiest person in the world, like really like a dream."

articles.body: El beticismo todavía conserva un regusto dulce cuando rememora el triunfo frente al Oporto en La Cartuja, perteneciente a la segunda fecha de la Champions League, mientras mira de reojo al partido de mañana frente al Barcelona en la capital hispalense. Los de Pellegrini han demostrado que no se arrugan en ningún escenario y llega el líder. Partidazo. Respecto a Álvaro Valles, que compite con Courtois (Real Madrid), Allison Becker (Liverpool), Haikin (Bodo Glimt) y Gregor Kobel (Borussia Dortmund), UEFA destaca una espectacular parada a una mano tras un cabezazo de Santiago Giménez en el tiempo de alargue para darle la victoria al Betis.

articles.title: Álvaro Benito identifica los males del Madrid y ofrece la solución: "Hay que tomar decisiones drásticas"
articles.standfirst: "Es la crónica de una muerte anunciada. Si no se cambian las cosas se reproducen los mismos problemas"
articles.summary: "Es la crónica de una muerte anunciada. Si no se cambian las cosas se reproducen los mismos problemas"
articles.body: Álvaro Benito, futbolista del Real Madrid de 1995 a 2002 que se vio obligado a retirarse del fútbol en 2003 por culpa de las lesiones, mostró en el programa 'El Larguero' la solución al juego del Real Madrid. "Es la crónica de una muerte anunciada. Si no se cambian las cosas se reproducen los mismos problemas. El partido del Real Madrid en Roma no pilla por sorpresa a nadie. Les cuesta mucho robar la pelota contra rivales que tienen muy trato de balón. Si permites a los rivales llegar con tanta facilidad alguna te van a acertar", compartió con Manu Carreño en la Cadena SER. Álvaro Benito cree que "Mourinho se desnudó" tácticamente en Roma y que los problemas del Madrid pueden venir por la gestión y reparto de responsabilidades sobre el terreno de juego: "Todos los futbolistas profesionales pueden correr sin balón. Tus vecinos, con los que te tienes que jugar las habichuelas tanto en España como en Europa, lo hacen. Todos vemos cuales son los problemas del Real Madrid, como no lo van a ver los jugadores y Mourinho... Podría tener un mediocentro de mejor pie, pero el Real Madrid tiene una pedazo de plantilla". El exfutbolista defiende que "habría que tomar decisiones drásticas que no sé si se van a dar". "A veces cumplir con los servicios mínimos es indispensable para poder ganar contra rivales de nivel. Fue un punto de inflexión, se vio que cuando presionan, le echan garra y aprietan obtienen resultados", dijo Álvaro Benito en un análisis que reproduce la web oficial de la SER. Álvaro Benito cree que "con Valverde y Tchouaméni no da". "Las declaraciones de Mourinho fueron muy interesantes, mostró el por qué hace las cosas. Sabe que tiene a jugadores que no son animales defensivos, por eso piensa que si no pone a Tchouaméni y a Valverde en el doble pivote, el equipo se le cae. Pero para controlar el juego lo tiene que hacer a través de futbolistas como Bernardo o Güler. No da puntada sin hilo en los mensajes que quiere dar", compartió. "Si los de arriba no hacen su función, Con Valverde y Tchouaméni contra equipos buenos no te da" y "si hay dos o tres jugadores en el equipo que no cumplen con sus funciones defensivas... igual en liga te da en el 80% de los partidos, pero en Champions te van a pintar la cara", insistió.

articles.title: Chirino antepuso el Almería a un Mundial con Curazao
articles.standfirst: El lateral neerlandés desvela que rechazó jugar con la selección caribeña durante la fase clasificatoria para centrarse en el ascenso
articles.summary: El lateral neerlandés desvela que rechazó jugar con la selección caribeña durante la fase clasificatoria para centrarse en el ascenso
articles.body: Daijiro Chirino atraviesa un gran momento de forma en la UD Almería. El lateral derecho viene de marcar su primer gol de la temporada ante el Leganés, confirmando el crecimiento que ha experimentado tras un inicio de curso algo irregular y un verano marcado por los rumores de mercado, con el interés de clubes como Valencia, Osasuna o Rayo Vallecano. El sistema de García Pimienta parece potenciar las principales virtudes del neerlandés. Con un equipo más sólido y mejor protegido en fase defensiva, Chirino puede explotar una de sus mayores cualidades: su constante proyección ofensiva. Una faceta que ya dejó patente la pasada campaña, cuando firmó tres goles, y que este curso ya ha comenzado a rentabilizar. El Almería apostó fuerte por él en el verano de 2025, desembolsando cerca de dos millones de euros para incorporarlo desde el Castellón. Con sólo 24 años y un evidente margen de crecimiento, el club considera que todavía está lejos de alcanzar su techo. No en vano, durante el pasado mercado rechazó todas las propuestas que llegaron por el futbolista, al que valora en torno a los 15 millones de euros. Su progresión también ha reabierto la posibilidad de dar el salto al panorama internacional. Nacido en Zwolle (Países Bajos) y con doble nacionalidad gracias a las raíces caribeñas de sus padres, Chirino desveló tras el encuentro frente al Leganés que Curazao llamó a su puerta antes de la fase de clasificación para el último Mundial. Sin embargo, decidió permanecer en Almería para centrarse exclusivamente en el objetivo del ascenso. "No es que esté esperando para jugar con Holanda. Curazao me preguntó para jugar, pero hablé con mi representante y quería estar en Almería para ayudar al equipo. No estoy pensando ya en una carrera con Holanda o Curazao", explicó el lateral. El defensa aseguró, además, que esa posibilidad continúa abierta y que sigue valorándola junto a su representante. De momento, todavía no ha debutado con ninguna selección absoluta, por lo que mantiene la opción de representar tanto a Curazao como, aunque con muchas menos posibilidades, a Países Bajos, país con el que fue internacional en las categorías sub 17 y sub 18 en 2019. Cuando volvió a ser preguntado sobre si había antepuesto el Almería a la posibilidad de disputar un Mundial con Curazao, Chirino quiso matizar la situación: "Antes del Mundial no fui a los partidos clasificatorios con Curazao y, cuando llegó el momento de jugarlo, ya no volvieron a preguntarme". Lo que sí parece evidente es que el lateral priorizó su crecimiento en el Almería sabiendo que existía la posibilidad de disputar una Copa del Mundo, un escaparate único para cualquier futbolista. En el caso de Países Bajos, además, la competencia en su demarcación es enorme, con jugadores del nivel de Denzel Dumfries o Jeremie Frimpong, lo que convierte una hipotética llamada en un desafío mucho mayor. Mientras tanto, Chirino sigue centrado en el presente. Su rendimiento ha dado un salto de calidad en este inicio de temporada y, si mantiene esta línea, no sólo puede convertirse en una pieza clave para el ascenso del Almería, sino también llamar definitivamente la atención en el panorama internacional como pasó en su día con Marc Pubill.

Chirino, en un partido del Almería.

articles.title: Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia still on, organisers say, but golf tour postponed
articles.summary: Asian Cup preparations continue for January, but Asian Tour delays golf’s Saudi Invitational after Houthi attacks.
articles.body:
The Asian Cup football tournament is on track to take place in Saudi Arabia early next year, local organisers say, but golf’s Asian Tour has postponed the Saudi International indefinitely in the aftermath of a series of attacks on Riyadh.

Yemen’s Houthi group claimed responsibility for the deadliest attack, which took place on Saturday on Riyadh’s international airport. It killed 14 people and ⁠wounded more than 300.

Australia also withdrew its team from the urban cycling World Championships on Friday, citing safety concerns over travelling to Riyadh, where the event is scheduled to take place in early November.

The Six Kings Slam exhibition tennis tournament in Riyadh has already been moved from October to December while FIFA on Thursday postponed the FIFAe Finals 2026 video game competition in ‌Jeddah until an unspecified future date.

In that environment, serious questions were being asked about whether the 24-team Asian Cup could still go ahead in Saudi Arabia from January 7 to February 5.

Three Saudi Pro League matches, including one featuring Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr , were postponed this week while Al-Nassr’s Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League game on Monday was delayed by an hour after Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence said it had intercepted a missile fired towards Riyadh.

AFC chief Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa said earlier this week that a postponement of the continental championships until 2028 was possible if necessary, but the local organising committee (LOC) said on Friday that it was sticking to the original schedule.

“Preparations across all organisational and operational areas are progressing according to the approved schedule, including work on venues, facilities ⁠and supporting services,” it said in a statement.

The LOC “will continue to monitor developments ⁠relevant to the tournament and ensure the appropriate conditions are in place for its successful delivery”.

Attacks in Saudi Arabia disrupt sport calendar

The $5m Saudi International, which is sponsored by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), is the flagship event on the Asian Tour and had been scheduled to take place at Riyadh ⁠Golf Club on November 18-21.

“The decision to postpone was taken following an assessment of the organisational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament and ensuring the event is ⁠delivered to a standard befitting its international stature,” an Asian Tour statement ⁠said.

AusCycling said its decision to withdraw the Australian team from the urban World Championships was made “with the safety and wellbeing of our athletes and staff our highest priority”.

The Australian government is advising travellers to “reconsider” trips to Saudi Arabia in general and Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport in particular “due to recent ‌security incidents”.

The Saudi government has invested heavily in sport through the PIF in recent years, and the Asian Cup was pitched as an early rehearsal for hosting football’s FIFA World Cup in 2034.

articles.title: Lisandro, asunto cerrado: reunión con la cúpula del United y disculpas: "Soy una persona apasionada..."
articles.standfirst: El centro argentino publica un segundo comunicado con el único fin de zanjar la crisis generada por sus palabras tras el choque contra el Atlético de Madrid
articles.summary: El centro argentino publica un segundo comunicado con el único fin de zanjar la crisis generada por sus palabras tras el choque contra el Atlético de Madrid
articles.body: La tormenta desatada por las explosivas declaraciones de Lisandro Martínez tras la derrota del Manchester United ante el Atlético parece empezar a remitir. Después del primer comunicado en el que reconocía haber hablado "desde el enojo y la frustración", el central argentino ha publicado un nuevo mensaje en sus redes sociales en el que revela que ya se ha reunido con la dirección del club y con el entrenador para rebajar la tensión. "Hoy me reuní con los dirigentes del club y con el entrenador. Fue una conversación muy positiva", explica el defensa en un texto en el que vuelve a asumir responsabilidades por sus palabras. El argentino admite que la frustración por la derrota le llevó a expresar sus sentimientos "en un momento y un lugar que quizá no fueron los correctos" y pide disculpas por ello. El mensaje supone un cambio de tono significativo respecto a las declaraciones realizadas tras el encuentro europeo, cuando sus críticas a la situación deportiva del club provocaron un fuerte revuelo en Inglaterra. Posteriormente, el campeón del mundo ya había matizado sus palabras en un primer comunicado, asegurando que había hablado movido por la decepción del resultado y recalcando su compromiso con el United. Ahora va un paso más allá. "Nuestro club es mejor cuando estamos unidos" y "todos en el Manchester United están haciendo todo lo posible para alcanzar nuestra ambición compartida", señala en una declaración que muchos medios ingleses interpretan como un intento definitivo de cerrar el conflicto interno generado durante las últimas horas. La prensa británica ha destacado especialmente dos aspectos del nuevo mensaje: la reunión directa entre el jugador, la dirección deportiva y el técnico, y el hecho de que el propio Lisandro considere el asunto resuelto. De hecho, el argentino concluye asegurando que, con esta situación ya atrás, toda la plantilla está "completamente centrada en ganar juntos". En medio de una temporada marcada por la irregularidad y por la presión creciente sobre el entorno de Old Trafford, el internacional argentino ha optado por rebajar el ruido y enviar un mensaje de unidad. "Hoy me reuní con los dirigentes del club y con el entrenador. Fue una conversación muy positiva, en la que pudimos intercambiar puntos de vista y hablar abiertamente sobre lo que ocurrió después del partido del martes. Todos saben que soy una persona apasionada y que vivo el fútbol con una enorme intensidad. La frustración por la derrota me llevó a expresar cómo me sentía en un momento y en un lugar que quizás no fueron los adecuados, y por eso quiero disculparme. Nuestro club está en su mejor versión cuando estamos todos unidos, y reconozco que mis palabras en ese momento no ayudaron a ello. Sé que todas y cada una de las personas del Manchester United están haciendo todo lo posible para lograr nuestra ambición compartida: devolver a este club y a su afición el éxito que merecen. Con esta situación ya detrás de nosotros, estamos completamente centrados en ganar juntos."

articles.title: SE Dons: How the YouTube football sensation went from Sunday League to one win away from FA Cup first-round history
articles.summary: SE Dons: Don Strapzy and Alex Teniola speak to William Bitibiri at Sky Sports as the club that started as a Sunday League team on YouTube chase FA Cup history; Beat Sholing on Satuday and they reach the first round proper, with Leicester among potential opponents
articles.body:
For years, Don Strapzy has said it while watching the SE Dons, his words becoming part of the soundtrack to a football club built on ambition, personality and a belief that the game belongs to everybody.

But when Alex Teniola scored in the 95th minute to complete a remarkable comeback against Chichester, the phrase found a new audience. The Dons had trailed 2-1 before scoring twice in added time to win 3-2. Don Strapzy's commentary went viral, capturing the kind of footballing drama that needs no embellishment.

There was more to come. A 5-1 victory away to former National League club Weymouth followed, leaving the Dons one win away from the FA Cup first round proper.

Three seasons ago, they were playing Sunday League football. Now, after six matches in their maiden FA Cup campaign, including a replay, they prepare to face Sholing in the fourth qualifying round, with Leicester City, Sheffield Wednesday or Reading among the clubs waiting in the next round.

The Dons have already beaten four teams from higher leagues. They are one of only three clubs left in the competition to have started in the extra preliminary round.

This is not supposed to happen. But then, the Dons have never been particularly interested in what is supposed to happen.

"We are just normal people that dare to be great," Don Strapzy told Sky Sports .

The club, founded in 2014 by south-east London rapper Don Strapzy, real name Andrew McHugh, and his friends, has grown from a Sunday League team into a football club, a content platform and a community with more than 250,000 YouTube subscribers.

The videos have taken supporters inside dressing rooms, onto touchlines and into the lives of the people who make the club what it is. In 2024, a link-up with Forest Hill Park opened the door to Saturday football. Promotion followed, and the SE Dons name was adopted for the 2025/26 campaign.

Their FA Cup debut arrived in August. A 2-0 victory against Erith Town at their home ground, The Garrison, announced their arrival in the competition.

Now, the dream is becoming difficult to contain.

"I used to speak to my dad about this all the time," Don Strapzy said. "My dad, he'd have a Guinness, and we'd get carried away. Like, 'Son, we're going to get to round three, get Man Utd.'

"And I'd be like, 'Dad, we're getting carried away'."

That conversation carries a different weight now. His father, known affectionately as Mr Old Skool, has since passed. So has his mother, Paula, who was a familiar presence around the club and helped with the kits.

"It's allowed me to keep my parents' names alive," Don Strapzy said. "My mum, anything for Paula. People that haven't met her, I hear my mum's name all the time.

"My dad, Mr Old Skool, he was a gentleman. He genuinely loved the club."

Don Strapzy explained that, after losing Paula, the club gave his father something to look forward to each week. Now, the shirts bearing Mr Old Skool's name and the supporters singing for him in the 70th minute offer a way for his son to honour that legacy.

His faith, too, is central to the story.

"My life could have gone so differently," he said. "I've got friends who are gone. They ain't coming back.

"My life could have gone in that route if it wasn't for my father, my mum, and my faith in the Lord."

For all the jokes about European football, the ambition is sincere. Don Strapzy has no intention of pretending otherwise.

"If we manage to beat Sholing, I'm asking myself, do we want the big tie now? Or do we try and get one that we can potentially go through?" he said.

"The way God is writing this script right now, I wouldn't be surprised if we get to round three."

The Europa League, meanwhile, has already entered the conversation.

"We've been dreaming big from the start," he said on Sky Sports News . "If we can win the FA Cup, we'll be in Europa League next season."

Tongue firmly in cheek, perhaps. But the Dons have earned the right to dream.

Teniola knows better than most what that belief looks like from the other side. Before joining the club, the forward played for Baiteeze Squad, one of the Dons' great Sunday League rivals. He described their rivalry as the Man Utd-Arsenal of that level, with hundreds turning out for matches that helped make grassroots football a spectacle again.

Yet when the opportunity came to join the Dons, Teniola recognised something familiar.

"I've always been a SE Dons sort of player," he said. "I wear my heart on my sleeve. And that's the kind of culture that's bred at SE Dons."

His late winner against Chichester was a reminder of why he fits. Introduced in the 85th minute, he kept his composure to toe-poke the ball under the goalkeeper and send his team-mates into celebration.

"I can never explain the feeling of scoring a winner," he said. "It's one of the best feelings in the world."

The goal also carried a personal significance. Teniola's nickname, "Teniola Time", dates back to a late goal for Tonbridge Angels around a decade ago. His latest intervention has given the name another chapter.

For Don Strapzy, the importance of the right characters goes beyond goals.

"You're not just a football player," he said. "You need the right characters in your changing room, the right leaders, the right mentality."

Big G, the club's long-serving captain and goalkeeper, understands that better than most. George Kamurasi is of royal lineage in Uganda's Tooro Kingdom and is often heard on a matchday bellowing the Dons spirit from between the sticks.

His story reflects the extraordinary lives behind the badge. His own grief, including the death of his parents, has also helped shape a club where remembrance and belonging are never far from the surface.

"What you see on camera is real," Teniola said. "No one is acting."

That authenticity is the Dons' greatest asset. The Viking-style celebrations, the music, the travelling support and the catchphrases may have helped them build an audience, but the football is now matching the spectacle.

Don Strapzy is under no illusion about what comes next. Sholing are two divisions above the Dons and have their own FA Cup dream to protect. There will be no overlooking them.

But a place in the first round proper would put a club born in Sunday League football alongside teams with Premier League histories. For a group that once dreamed of taking on Manchester United over a drink and a conversation, that would be something.

"It's history, bro," Don Strapzy said. "We're literally making history."

The Dons have spent years building their boat to conquer new shores. One more victory could take them somewhere they have never been before.

And if Teniola finds himself in the right place at the right time again, perhaps the commentary will take care of itself.

Some things don't need commentary. Some things just need to be seen.

articles.title: Clara Serrajordi, nominada para el Golden Girl
articles.standfirst: La jugadora del Barcelona está entre las diez candidatas junto a sus compañeras Sydney Schertenleib o Giulia Galli, amén de la madridista Felicia Schröder
articles.summary: La jugadora del Barcelona está entre las diez candidatas junto a sus compañeras Sydney Schertenleib o Giulia Galli, amén de la madridista Felicia Schröder
articles.body: Clara Serrajordi, jugadora del Barcelona e internacional con la selección española, forma parte de las diez candidatas al Golden Girl, prestigioso premio que concede Tuttosport a las mejores jugadoras Sub'21 de equipos europeos y que coronó en el pasado a Jule Brand (2022), Linda Caicedo (2023), Vicky López (2024) y Michelle Agyemang (2025). La centrocampista del Barcelona, también nominada para el 'Premio a Mejor Jugadora Joven' en el Balón de Oro, parte entre las principales favoritas al Golden Girl. Serrajordi ha logrado hacerse un hueco en un equipo como el Barcelona, campeón de todo (Liga, Copa, Supercopa de España y Champions League) el curso pasado, y en la selección absoluta con la que conquistó la Nations League y se clasificó para el Mundial de Brasil del próximo verano. Junto a Clara, otras dos jugadoras del Barcelona aparecen en la lista de finalistas: Sydney Schertenleib, talento suizo también asentado en el primer equipo del Barcelona y en la absoluta de su país; y Giulia Galli, uno de los últimos fichajes de las azulgrana con protagonismo hasta ahora en el filial. Además, Felicia Schröder, jugadora del Real Madrid, es otro de los rostros conocidos por el gran público de nuestro país que aparece en el listado. La internacional sueca, campeona de la Europa Cup el curso pasado con el BK Häcken y protagonista de uno de los mayores traspasos en la historia del mal llamado fútbol femenino (se estima que su fichaje por el club blanco rondó el millón y medio de euros) también se postula entre las candidatas. La lista la completan la la suiza Iman Beney, del Manchester City; la neerlandesa Veerle Buurman, del Chelsea; la francesa Maeline Mendy, del Paris FC; la italiana Azzurra Gallo, del Toulouse; la sueca Smilla Holmberg, del Arsenal; y la alemana Alara Şehitler, del Bayern de Múnich. La ganadora del premio será anunciada el próximo mes de noviembre.

articles.title: Chelsea's Reece James out for three months after knee surgery
articles.summary: Chelsea captain Reece James is set to miss three months of action after undergoing knee surgery.
articles.body:
Chelsea captain Reece James is set to miss three months of action after undergoing knee surgery.

The defender, 26, was injured in training before Chelsea 's 5-1 win over Bournemouth last weekend, and the decision was taken for him to have surgery.

James is now undergoing rehabilitation with Chelsea 's medical staff, with no time-frame given for his return.

Chelsea next travel to Everton in the Premier League before hosting London rivals Tottenham and Manchester United in a difficult run of fixtures. A trip to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup is sandwiched between those two home matches.

James has suffered multiple injuries over the past few seasons, causing him to miss several international tournaments with England since the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

His injury record improved significantly last season, allowing him to play a prominent role in England's World Cup campaign, during which they reached the semi-finals before winning the bronze medal match.

James was among the players to withdraw from England duty during the most recent international break. The next international break begins at the start of November, when England are scheduled to face Croatia at Wembley Stadium.

articles.summary: El torneo continental reunirá a jugadores como Kang In (Atlético) o
articles.body: Arabia Saudí sigue siendo sacudida estos días por el conflicto que acecha la zona, pero el Comité organizador de la Copa Asia 2027 (7 enero-5 febrero) confirmó hoy que continúan, de forma normal, los preparativos para el torneo continental que agrupará a grandes figuras del fútbol asiático. El Comité Local de Organización (LOC) de la Copa Asiática de la AFC Arabia Saudí confirma que los preparativos para el torneo siguen según lo previsto. El trabajo continúa en estrecha coordinación con la Confederación Asiática de Fútbol (AFC) y otros actores relevantes. Recordemos que el conflicto que acecha a Saudi, Yemen y otros países de la zona han causado, por ejemplo, al menos 19 muertos, incluidos extranjeros, en más de una semana de ataques hutíes dirigidos contra el aeropuerto internacional de Riad, la sede del gigante petrolero saudí Aramco y otras instalaciones aeronáuticas, petroleras y militares en todo el reino. "Los preparativos -dice el comunicado- en todas las áreas organizativas y operativas avanzan según el calendario aprobado, incluyendo el trabajo en recintos, instalaciones y servicios de apoyo. El objetivo sigue siendo ofrecer una experiencia de torneo de clase mundial para los equipos participantes, aficionados y medios de comunicación de toda Asia, reuniendo al continente a través del fútbol". "La LOC sigue comprometida a mantener los preparativos en marcha y a garantizar que se dispongan de los recursos necesarios para ofrecer un torneo que refleje las ambiciones y estándares de Arabia Saudí como anfitrión. Al mismo tiempo, seguirá supervisando los desarrollos relevantes para el torneo y asegurándose de que existan las condiciones adecuadas para su exitosa realización. El Ministerio de Energía de Arabia Saudí, por ejemplo, confirmó que el impacto de un misil balístico contra el complejo de la sede de ARAMCO en Dhahran. Los problemas siguen, pero la Copa Asia, también.

articles.title: Powerchair Football World Cup 2026: England among the favourites
articles.summary: Colin Gordon will be coaching Argentina at the World Cup, while son Chris will be  playing for England.
articles.body:
"I was a big football fan growing up. My dad got involved with powerchair football through me," England goalkeeper Chris Gordon says of his father Colin.

"But he's now coaching Argentina, so we'll be facing each other in the World Cup."

For Gordon Jr, who is playing at his fourth Powerchair Football World Cup for England, Sunday's meeting with hosts Argentina carries extra significance with his dad in the opposite dugout in Buenos Aires.

Gordon Sr is himself a former professional footballer, a striker at clubs including Birmingham City, Fulham and Leicester City in the 1980s and 90s, who later became a football agent.

"My dad and I have worked together at West Brom for a number of years and then he coached me for the England national team," Chris says of their working relationship. But this one is more personal.

At the last World Cup in 2023, Colin managed England to the final, where they lost on penalties against France. But this time around, Chris is hoping to get one over his father.

"England will definitely come out on top [against Argentina], so bragging rights will be coming my way," the Kidderminster resident told BBC Sport.

Powerchair football, also known as power football or wheelchair football, is a four-a-side sport played by people with impairments including muscular dystrophy, cerebral palsy and spinal muscular atrophy.

All it requires is a basketball court, a bigger football and powerchairs with front bumpers on that allow players to shoot, pass and dribble the ball.

In England, the game has two top divisions in which teams from around the country compete. Hundreds of players also play in regional leagues around the country.

Leagues also exist in Scotland and across the island of Ireland, while teams are developing apace in Cardiff and Wrexham.

Over the next week, 10 teams - ranging from hosts Argentina and neighbours Uruguay to as far afield as Australia and Japan - will compete for the World Cup.

Games begin on Saturday, with the final on Friday 23 October. All matches will be streamed live on YouTube , external as teams compete to be crowned world champions.

England are among the favourites for this year's tournament - alongside France and the USA - and there's a real sense of optimism that they could bring the trophy back home.

The England squad has youth and experience.

Dan McLellan, 17, is preparing for his second World Cup, while England captain Jon Bolding is heading to his fifth.

"I've been playing powerchair football for 25 years now. Back in the day, we used to use our NHS wheelchair and just put car tyres round the front," said Bolding, who is from near Reading.

McLellan recently took over the captaincy of his club side, Aspire PFC, from Bolding.

"I've been playing since I was eight years old. I got into the [England] squad at 14," the winger, who is from Peterborough, said.

"It's not every 17-year-old that gets to two major tournaments, but I try to maintain my level and improve on it.

"We believe in ourselves to get to that final. We've got enough to do it this time," he said.

Bolding added: "It would mean so much to bring [the World Cup] home for England. We've been trying for so many years now. We won the Euros in 2019; this is the only thing that we're missing."

Head coach Adam McEvoy is hopeful the side can go one better than they did three years ago.

"I'm really looking forward to this World Cup to showcase how we play, who we are, and our style of football [but] it's going to be the toughest World Cup there has been so far," McEvoy said.

"With the group that we have and the way that we try and play, there's no reason we can't go very deep into the competition."

articles.title: Man Utd veering towards crisis as Man City cloud hangs over Premier League
articles.summary: Lisandro Martinez apologises for his criticism after on-field spotlight shifts to Manchester United from City.
articles.body:
Manchester United will travel to historic rivals Leeds for their next match as pressure mounts on manager Michael Carrick while Manchester City aim to extend their perfect Premier League start despite the uncertainty over their future.

Brighton could be one of the big winners should City suffer severe sanctions for breaking the Premier League’s financial rules.

The Seagulls are riding high, just two points behind second-placed Arsenal, before their grudge match on Sunday against Crystal Palace.

Martinez blast comes after Man Utd’s worst start for 40 years

United are off to their worst league start in 40 years and were plunged further into chaos by defender Lisandro Martinez’s attack on the club’s hierarchy over a lack of investment after Tuesday’s 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid .

The Argentinian took aim at Technical Director Jason Wilcox after the Red Devils added only three midfielders during the transfer window.

But Martinez himself has been one of those most culpable for a miserable start to the campaign for his part in goals conceded to Fulham and Tottenham in recent weeks.

United have won just one of their opening six league games and were also dumped out of the League Cup last month by Brighton.

Leeds last beat the Red Devils at Elland Road in 2002 but did inflict the only home defeat of Carrick’s interim spell in charge last season when the sides met in April.

Carrick is increasingly at risk of becoming the latest manager unable to turn around a sharp decline at Old Trafford since Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013.

But he said the hostile atmosphere that will await his side presents the perfect chance to bounce back.

“What a great game [on] Sunday to prepare for. It’s a fantastic game for us, for the club, for the history, for the supporters,” Carrick said.

“Everything to do with the game is a great game, so we’ll be ready for that.”

Martinez has since apologised for his comments .

Man City charges leave Premier League in limbo

Manchester City sit pretty at the top of the table with six wins from six league games, but that may all count for nothing if they do not successfully overturn a guilty verdict on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules.

Enzo Maresca’s men shut out that distraction to win 3-0 at Liverpool last weekend and rallied impressively in the second half despite losing 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in a thrilling Champions League tie on Tuesday.

But the uncertainty over their future has left the entire league in limbo.

City deny any wrongdoing , and a case that began eight years ago has at least a few months left to run before the appeal is heard and a potential sanction announced.

“My underlying thought is none of this is good for football and there are no winners,” former England manager Gareth Southgate said.

City can stretch their lead at the top to six points when Ipswich visit the Etihad on Saturday. Arsenal are not in action until 24 hours later at Nottingham Forest.

The football regulator in England said after City’s appeal that he expects an outcome by January .

‘Ruthless’ Brighton eye Champions League

Arsenal’s only defeat this season came in a 3-0 trouncing by Brighton, whose remarkable rise could reach new heights this season with many of the other established giants struggling.

Brighton have soared through the divisions and into Europe on the back of owner Tony Bloom’s expertise in data analytics.

But they are yet to play Champions League football.

Despite routinely selling their prized assets to wealthier clubs, Brighton’s smart recruitment of both players and coaches has allowed them to continue to thrive.

That has also made them a neutral’s favourite, but manager Fabian Hurzeler wants his side to show their nasty side against rivals Palace on Sunday.

“We want to be ruthless. We want to create this energetic atmosphere where it makes it so hard to come to this place,” Hurzeler said. “We have to keep building this together with our fans and not be the nice football club any more.”

articles.title: Otro gol pasado el minuto 60 y van ¡13 de 18!
articles.standfirst: La Real se dejó dos puntos muy valiosos con el postrero tanto de la USG y otros días ha visto como la heroica le ha salvado de perderlos por esas dianas al final
articles.summary: La Real se dejó dos puntos muy valiosos con el postrero tanto de la USG y otros días ha visto como la heroica le ha salvado de perderlos por esas dianas al final
articles.body: La Real Sociedad encajó el gol que le privó de ganar en Lovaina a la Union Saint-Gilloise en el minuto 88 y de los 18 que ha recibido en la decena de encuentros disputados en esta temporada ya son ¡13, un 72%! los llegados a partir de la hora de juego, así que parece que baja sus prestaciones defensivas, por el cansancio o la influencia de las sustituciones. El equipo txuriurdin sólo ha hecho cuatro de sus 14 dianas en esa fase, lo que quiere decir que suelen empezar por delante. La Real ya vio como en la jornada inaugural de LaLiga, ante el Betis en La Cartuja, recibió el que fue el 1-0 final en el minuto 63, encajando tres de los cuatro goles de la derrota por 4-1 en el Santiago Bernabéu frente al Real Madrid pasada la hora de juego. Pasados los choques contra el Espanyol y el Celta, el Elche igualó un 0-2 con dianas en el 67 y el 74 y el Atlético venció 0-3 marcando en los minutos 84, 90 y 95. El Bournemouth encarriló pronto su triunfo 1-2, pero después el Valencia, que había hecho un tanto en el 57, complicó el de la Real en el 84, aunque Barrenetxea marcó después. También hizo el Dépor goles en el 61 y 69, aunque la Real ganaba 3-0 y no supusieron males mayores como el de este jueves en Lovaina. Y es que el equipo de Matarazzo se adelantó nada más iniciarse la segunda parte y acarició su primer triunfo europeo durante muchos minutos, hasta que en el 88 la USG logró un empate doloroso para los txuriurdin, pero merecido para los locales, por los méritos de unos y otros durante los noventa y tantos minutos que duró el partido. Fue el decimotercer tanto que la Real encaja pasada la hora de juego, de los 18 que ha recibido, cuatro tan sólo antes del descanso, un dato que puede suponer que los encuentros se le hacen largos o que nota el cansancio o los desajustes que pueden producir los cambios de los entrenadores. El técnico de Nueva Jersey tendrá que lograr que su equipo alargue su buen rendimiento para evitar perder puntos, como en Bélgica, o tener que recurrir a la heroica para conservarlos, como frente a Elche y Valencia, casi con el Dépor.
