articles.title: Harry Kane agrees new Bayern Munich contract until 2029
articles.summary: England captain Harry Kane has agreed a new deal with Bayern Munich, extending his stay with the Bundesliga champions until 2029.According to the Daily Mail,...
articles.body:
England captain Harry Kane has agreed a new deal with Bayern Munich, extending his stay with the Bundesliga champions until 2029.

According to the Daily Mail , the 33-year-old striker has reached a verbal agreement on a new three-year contract, with the German champions now preparing the paperwork to make the deal official.

Kane has been in blistering form this year, bagging 50 goals and is among the leading contenders for the Ballon d'Or. His goalscoring form has also linked him with a big-money move to Barcelona.

However, the former Tottenham Hotspur has now agreed to continue his career in Germany after settling comfortably into life at Bayern.

Both Kane and the club had previously insisted there was no need to rush discussions over his future before the summer.

In May, Kane made it clear that he was happy at Bayern and wanted to focus on the season and the upcoming World Cup before making any decisions.

"It's not the time to talk about that now, but there's no panic," he said. "We wanted to hold conversations until the end of the season, and we've got a World Cup still to play.

"But everyone knows how much I enjoy it here. That situation is calm."

He has now backed up that claim by pledging his allegiance to the Bundesliga powerhouse .

Kane joined Bayern from Tottenham in 2023 in a deal worth around £100 million and is in the final year of his initial four-year contract.

However, there's no indication his new contract includes a pay rise on his current £400,000-a-week salary. Kane's decision reflects how well his family has settled in Germany.

Kane, his wife Kate and their four children moved from north London three years ago. The family has regularly been seen taking part in local activities, including Munich's famous Oktoberfest celebrations.

Meanwhile, Kane continues to deliver for club and country on the pitch. He has already scored eight goals in nine games across all competitions for Bayern.

articles.title: Spain punished by FIFA for Islamophobic chants during Egypt friendly
articles.summary: Spain sanctioned by FIFA after incidents at Espanyol’s stadium in Barcelona, which staged the friendly with Egypt.
articles.body:
Spain have ‌‌‌‌been fined $20,000 and ordered to partially close their stadium ⁠⁠⁠⁠for their ⁠⁠⁠⁠next friendly after supporters twice chanted Islamophobic slogans during the game against Egypt in March, FIFA said ⁠⁠⁠⁠in a statement.

The sanctions relate to incidents at the RCDE Stadium near Barcelona, home of LaLiga club Espanyol, ⁠⁠⁠⁠where some Spain fans chanted, “Who doesn’t jump is a Muslim” during a World Cup warm-up match which ended in a 0-0 draw.

After the second occurrence of the chant, the stadium announcer ‌‌‌‌issued a warning and the scoreboard displayed a message against discriminatory behaviour.

Spain winger Lamine Yamal, who is Muslim, condemned the chants at the time, describing them as disrespectful and intolerable and calling those responsible “ignorant and racist”.

Spanish police launched an investigation the following day, while world governing ⁠⁠⁠⁠body FIFA later started disciplinary proceedings against ⁠⁠⁠⁠the Spanish football federation (RFEF).

It argued that the word ‘Muslim’ was “neither insulting nor pejorative”, adding that the fans’ conduct should be assessed under FIFA’s Article 17, ⁠⁠⁠⁠which covers political, ideological, religious or offensive messages, rather than Article 15, which deals ⁠⁠⁠⁠with discrimination and racist abuse.

However, FIFA’s disciplinary ⁠⁠⁠⁠committee rejected that argument, saying Article 15 does not require the explicit use of a slur and that a term can be discriminatory when ‌‌‌‌used in context as “an insult, taunt, or marker of inferiority”.

FIFA fined the RFEF and ordered the closure of at least ‌‌‌‌15% ‌‌‌‌of available seats for Spain’s next friendly.

Al Jazeera has contacted the RFEF for comment.

articles.title: Lisandro Martinez: Man Utd defender in squad for Leeds trip as Michael Carrick insists situation resolved
articles.summary: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick insists Lisandro Martinez situation has been resolved and the defender realises "he made a mistake" by criticising the club's hierarchy after Tuesday's defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League
articles.body:
Head coach Michael Carrick insisted the situation is resolved and that "we have moved on" in a press conference dominated by questions about Martinez after he called out director of football Jason Wilcox over a lack of investment in the transfer window.

Martinez, whose outspoken comments came after Tuesday's 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, met the club's hierarchy, including Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, and Carrick, on Thursday before making an apology.

Asked about Martinez on Friday ahead of Sunday's trip to Leeds, live on Sky Sports , Carrick said: "He's released his statement and realised he made a mistake.

"That's enough for us to move on with. From our point of view, the acknowledgement of what's been done is enough to move on."

United legends Wayne Rooney and Gary Neville have criticised Martinez for his comments, questioning what impact it might have on the club's dressing room.

But Carrick, who is under mounting pressure with United on a five-game winless run, was adamant that the spirit of the group remains strong ahead of two tough away games against Leeds and Como.

"We've moved on from that," said the United boss. "As a group we've moved on. It's really not a drama for the group. The squad have trained really well and they are in good spirits.

"It was pretty simple. We understood the situation. Licha understood he made a mistake. We have a really good feeling from the club. Results-wise it hasn't gone our way, but the spirit and togetherness. We can see in the group we want to do something with this situation.

"We've moved on. Genuinely. There is a freshness about the group."

Questioned on why people would believe that the squad has remained unified after Martinez's outburst, Carrick added: ""There's a lot of people saying a lot of things. Pros and ex-pros, that doesn't mean they know what's going on here.

"The players totally believe me. Just because people talk on the outside doesn't make it the truth. I am telling you the truth.

"The squad [on Friday] was in a fantastic place, better than I've seen it for a while, actually. It's plain and simple.

"It's not affected [the spirit], I'm telling you. We're in a good place."

Analysis: Carrick handled situation well – but talking needs to be on the pitch

"As a player, Michael Carrick was unflustered and calm.

"In Friday's press conference, he has been no different. He offered a straight bat to the inevitable questions about Martinez and only seem ruffled when it was suggested that he needed a result against Leeds - "we need a result" interjected the United head coach.

"Ultimately, though, United's talking needs to be on the pitch. And if there was one jarring note in the presser, it was Carrick's insistence that all is well at United that stood out. United are not, in his words, "in a good place". They can only be if they arrest their alarming slump in form, starting at Leeds on Sunday."

Sky Sports News' Football Correspondent Rob Dorsett :

There are real doubts about whether Martinez's contract will be extended when it expires in the summer.

Manchester United will focus on revamping their defence in the next transfer windows and have the formal option to prolong Martinez's stay for a further year.

Sky Sports News has been told United are looking at new centre-backs, as well as left-backs.

It is also understood that there is no pressure on Wilcox internally regarding his position.

Martinez has been keen on a move away from Old Trafford for some time.

In the summer, he pushed for a move to Atletico Madrid, the side that beat United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, to follow his good friend and international team-mate, Cristian Romero, who left Spurs for Spain.

No suitable bid for Martinez came in for Manchester United to consider.

The 28-year-old made similar explosive comments about his bosses when at Ajax in 2022. Martinez, who again wanted a move away, called their sporting director Gerry Hamstra a "nobody".
